activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Displacement of a Particle Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=2t+{t}^{2}.$ At time $t=1$ the particle is located at the position $x=4.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=3?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=3$ is equal to its position at $t=1$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [1,3].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(3)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{3}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(3) & =4+{\int }_{1}^{3}(2t+{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =4+{[{t}^{2}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =4+([{3}^{2}+\frac{{3}^{3}}{3}]-[{1}^{2}+\frac{{1}^{3}}{3}]) \\  & =4+([9+9]-[1+\frac{1}{3}]) \\  & =4+(18-\frac{4}{3}) \\  & =4+\frac{50}{3} \\  & =\frac{62}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=3$ is $x=\frac{62}{3}.$
